misconception_description: Student believes that the body of an if-statement executes repeatedly as long as the condition holds.

solutions.generated_code:
program HitungKemunculanStd
kamus
  s : string
  i, jumlah : integer
algoritma
  input(s)
  jumlah <- 0
  i <- 1
  if i <= panjang(s) - 2 then
    if s[i] == 's' and s[i+1] == 't' and s[i+2] == 'd' then
      jumlah <- jumlah + 1
    endif
    i <- i + 1
  endif
  output(jumlah)
endprogram

metadata.modification_notes: The student replaced the for loop with an if-statement, believing that the if-statement will repeatedly execute its body as long as the condition `i < len(s) - 2` remains true. They expect that after incrementing `i`, the if-statement will automatically re-evaluate and continue checking subsequent positions in the string, similar to how a while loop would behave. In reality, the if-statement executes only once, so the code will only check position 0 of the string and return at most 1 (or 0 if 'std' is not at the beginning). This demonstrates the misconception that if-statements loop like while-statements.
